newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish debt ended lower on Wednesday, despite coming off previous lows as the bond future bounced back to an important resistance, dealers said.
"The American market was pulling bonos down, when the market bounced back before breaking big resistance at 113.50," a dealer in Madrid said, adding that the market had very light volume.
The 10-year spread was back below 100 basis points, after having traded above that level during the day.
"Spain's tone is very positive. If foreign markets remain quiet we'll be able to gain more from here," a dealer added.
"Bonos were influenced only a bit by the U.S. Treasuries' fall, and that's a very good signal," another dealer added.
The yield curve was almost unchanged, with the two- to 10-year bond spread at around 130 basis points from 128 bps at the close yesterday evening.
At today's auction, one-year bills were allotted with a fall in yield to 5.347 percent versus 5.590 percent. -- Madrid Newsroom, + 341 585 8340
